discovery: Programmable arrays of individual neutral atoms controlled through Rydberg interactions, used for quantum simulation and quantum information processing

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique Graduate School, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum science
motivation: The nominees made single neutral atoms, held in optical tweezers and coupled through Rydberg interactions, into one of the most powerful platforms of the second quantum revolution. Saffman and Browaeys (with Grangier) first showed Rydberg blockade between two individually trapped atoms in 2009 and used it to entangle them and build quantum gates. Lukin proposed the blockade mechanism and later led the move to large programmable arrays. Browaeys and Lukin built defect-free, reconfigurable arrays of hundreds of atoms. With them they made quantum simulators of many-body spin models that resolve new phases, including topological spin liquids and quantum phase transitions beyond classical computation. Lukin and his collaborators also demonstrated error-corrected logical qubits. This work is elegant optics and control of individual quantum particles. It has turned entanglement from a subject of foundational tests into an engineering resource at scale.
